name: Sea-Stair Landing
read: The sea-stair ends at a long landing of wet grey stone, held up by two thick pillars. Two crates of supplies stand by the wall, marked with red hobgoblin paint, beside a coil of rope with a grappling hook and a lantern. A dented iron helmet and a broken spear lie on the floor among shells and strands of seaweed. Two burial urns lie smashed open, their ashes trodden into the wet stone.
notes:
Where the sea-stair from the cove comes up into the sepulcher. The hobgoblins landed here a month ago and left their spare supplies by the door; their longship, the Red Wake, lies beached in the cove below. The helmet belonged to a hobgoblin dragged off by the crabs of the Drowned Chapel (room 4). The rest of the sepulcher is dark unless a room says otherwise.

No encounter. The 4 Hobgoblin Shieldbearers in the Flooded Antechamber (room 2) hear any fighting or loud noise here and are ready behind their barricade.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing in one of the hobgoblin supply crates, wrapped in a dead hobgoblin's red sash.

Exits: Flooded Antechamber (2, door). The double doors in the middle of the south side lead out and down the sea-stair to the cove. The door at the south end of the west side opens into the middle of the east side of the Flooded Antechamber.

name: Flooded Antechamber
read: Seawater stands ankle-deep across much of this antechamber. Two stone benches have been overturned into a low barricade facing the east doorway, lined with red-painted shields, and hobgoblins crouch behind it. A rack of spears leans on a wall beside a cold iron brazier, wet sacks and a bucket. Through the south archway a passage runs on into the dark, and farther down it fresh rubble lies on the floor under a cracked ceiling.
notes:
The hobgoblins' guard post, holding the way in for the warband camped in the Hall of the Fallen Legion (room 5). The water is shallow; it costs no extra movement.

Encounter: 4 Hobgoblin Shieldbearers hold the barricade (half cover) and lock shields against anyone coming through the east door, fighting until two fall, when the rest fall back through the south archway to warn Vrask. Talk: they want to hold their post and fear Vrask more than the party; a character who claims to come with terms for the Warlord and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) check gets them to lower their spears and lead the party to room 5 by the north door.

Trap: the passage south from the south archway holds the Collapsing Passage (see room 5). The hobgoblins know it and use the passage east to room 5's north door; a captured or talked-round hobgoblin warns of it.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Sea-Stair Landing (1, door), Hall of Offerings (3, stairs and stairs), Drowned Chapel (4, stairs and open passage), Monk's Grotto (9, stairs, barred gate and arch), Hall of the Fallen Legion (5, arch and door), Guardian Antechamber (10, arch and door). The door in the middle of the east side opens into the south end of the west side of the Sea-Stair Landing. The stairs in the middle of the north side climb to a passage north. After 20 ft a barred iron gate on its west side (barred from this side; lifting the bar takes an action) opens onto a passage that runs west, south and west again to an arch into the middle of the east side of the Monk's Grotto. The passage north goes on through an open passage to a junction: stairs east climb into the middle of the west side of the Hall of Offerings, and an open passage west leads into the middle of the east side of the Drowned Chapel. The arch in the middle of the south side opens onto a passage south to a flooded east–west corridor. West, it runs to a passage south that ends at a door into the middle of the north side of the Guardian Antechamber. East, it runs to a passage south that ends at a door into the middle of the north side of the Hall of the Fallen Legion. Straight south, the long passage (Collapsing Passage) ends at a door into the north end of the west side of the Hall of the Fallen Legion.

name: Hall of Offerings
read: A low stone altar stands against the north wall of this small hall, laid with dried flowers, green coins and candle stubs. Along the east wall runs a row of clay offering pots, and above them narrow slits are cut into the stone. The floor in front of the pots is pocked and chipped, and old dried blood is spattered up the wall beneath the slits. A bronze candlestick lies toppled by a cracked bowl.
notes:
Islanders left gifts here for the King's spirit. The tide-monks set spears behind the slits so that no thief would take the offerings in the pots. The coins on the altar are corroded copper, worth nothing.

Trap: Offering Slits

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 5-ft strip along the east wall, under the slits above the offering pots (the whole 30 ft of it).
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices the dried blood and the pocked stone under the slits, and the glint of spear points in the dark behind them.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 piercing]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Prone condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam the slits with cloth or wedges (DC 15 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), or keep to the west side of the room.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Embalmers' Room (6, door), Drowned Chapel (4, stairs and open passage), Flooded Antechamber (2, stairs and stairs), Monk's Grotto (9, stairs, barred gate and arch). The door in the middle of the north side opens into the middle of the south side of the Embalmers' Room. The stairs in the middle of the west side go down to a junction: an open passage west leads into the middle of the east side of the Drowned Chapel, and a passage south runs past a barred gate west (to the Monk's Grotto, see room 2) and down stairs into the middle of the north side of the Flooded Antechamber.

name: Drowned Chapel
read: Two short stone pews face a broken lectern and a cracked stone font in this small burial chapel. Bones and skulls lie heaped along the walls under a fallen stone shelf, tangled with seaweed. Empty crab shells crunch underfoot everywhere. As you enter, the bone piles begin to shift and click.
notes:
A side chapel for the King's lesser dead. At high tide the sea comes up through the cracked font from the caves below, and with it the crabs, which have stripped every bone here and the hobgoblins who came in a month ago.

Encounter: 4 Gravecrawler Swarms burst from the bone piles and swarm the nearest creatures, fighting until destroyed. They are not intelligent and cannot be bargained with; thrown meat or a fallen body distracts one swarm for a round.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Ossuary of the Honour Guard (7, door), Hall of Offerings (3, open passage and stairs), Flooded Antechamber (2, open passage and stairs), Monk's Grotto (9, open passage, barred gate and arch). The door in the middle of the north side opens into the middle of the south side of the Ossuary of the Honour Guard. The open passage in the middle of the east side leads to a junction: stairs east climb into the middle of the west side of the Hall of Offerings, and a passage south runs past a barred gate west (to the Monk's Grotto, see room 2) and down stairs into the Flooded Antechamber.

name: Hall of the Fallen Legion
read: A campfire with a cooking spit burns in the middle of this great burial hall, and around it lie eight hobgoblin bedrolls. Six stone sarcophagi have been pushed against the north and south walls, their lids thrown off. Weapon racks, a map table and stool, an iron-bound war chest and heaps of tarnished bronze grave goods crowd the floor under a red war banner. In the middle of the east wall stands a huge bronze door, closed, with a clear space of floor before it.
notes:
The Legion's officers were buried here; the hobgoblins have emptied their sarcophagi and made it their camp. The campfire lights the whole hall. The huge bronze door in the east wall is locked. It opens when someone lays a hand on it and speaks the King's true name, Morvane (Brother Tamsin in room 9 knows it; the fresco in room 13 shows it). It can also be picked (DC 20 Dexterity check with thieves' tools) or forced (DC 22 Strength (Athletics) check). Vrask has no key; he has been trying to make the monk talk. Beyond the door, the first 20 ft of room 8 are trapped (Oathbreaker's Ring).

Encounter: Warlord Vrask Ironjaw, 1 Hobgoblin Devastator and 1 Hobgoblin Shieldbearer. The shieldbearer holds the door the party comes in by while the devastator blasts from behind the map table and Vrask goes for the strongest-looking character. Talk: Vrask wants the treasure behind the bronze door and fears losing face before his warband; a party that offers to open the door and let him take the first share, and succeeds on a DC 17 Charisma (Persuasion) check, gets a truce (he means to betray them in room 15), and a character who challenges him to single combat with a DC 15 Charisma (Intimidation) check gets a duel to the first to drop, his warband standing back.

Trap: Collapsing Passage

  • Trigger: a creature enters the 15 ft of the long north–south passage halfway between room 2's south archway and the door into the northwest of room 5.
  • Find: DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) notices fresh rubble on the floor and a cracked ceiling held up by a single loose keystone.
  • Effect: DC 15 Dexterity saving throw [[/save dex 15]]; [[/damage 10d10 bludgeoning]] on a failure, half on a success. On a failure the creature also has the Restrained condition, pinned under the stone until it or an ally uses an action and succeeds on a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check.
  • Disarm or avoid: Knock the keystone loose from outside the area (a ranged attack against AC 15, or a thrown heavy object), or use the untrapped passage to the north door of room 5.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

Treasure: 500 gp in Vrask's iron-bound war chest (locked; Vrask carries its key, or DC 15 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), a Potion of Healing on the map table, and Bracers of Archery in the heap of looted grave goods.

Exits: Hall of the Kneeling Knights (8, locked bronze door), Flooded Antechamber (2, door and arch, two ways), Guardian Antechamber (10, door and door). The huge locked bronze door in the middle of the east side opens into the middle of the west side of the Hall of the Kneeling Knights. The door in the middle of the north side opens onto a passage north to a flooded east–west corridor: west, it passes the arch into the south side of the Flooded Antechamber and the head of the Collapsing Passage, and runs on to a passage south that ends at a door into the north side of the Guardian Antechamber. The door at the north end of the west side opens onto the long north–south passage (Collapsing Passage), which runs north to the same corridor, just below the Flooded Antechamber's south arch.

name: Embalmers' Room
read: Two narrow stone tables stand in the middle of this workroom, stained dark with old oils. Shelves of clay jars line the walls, and rolls of yellowed linen wrappings are stacked beside a stone basin. Tools lie on a small table: hooks, knives and long needles. A canopic jar lies smashed on the floor.
notes:
The tide-monks prepared the King's dead here. The jars hold dried herbs, salts and resins; the smashed canopic jar held the heart of a Legion officer and is long empty.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Hall of Offerings (3, door), Chapel of the Tide (11, arch and open passage). The door in the middle of the south side opens into the middle of the north side of the Hall of Offerings. The arch in the middle of the east side opens onto a passage east that ends at an open passage into the middle of the west side of the Chapel of the Tide.

name: Ossuary of the Honour Guard
read: Bones and skulls are stacked in niches up every wall of this ossuary. Three stone biers stand along the west wall, and on each lies a skeleton in old armour. Rusted round shields and spears lean against the walls, and dust and broken bone cover the floor. As you step in, the three armoured dead sit up on their biers.
notes:
The Fallen Legion's captains lie here. They still keep the oath that their King broke, and guard his sepulcher from all comers.

Encounter: 3 Barrow Wights rise from the biers and fight shoulder to shoulder, shields locked, until destroyed. A wight must succeed on a DC 15 Wisdom saving throw to attack the wearer of the Fallen King's Signet first. Talk: they want their oath kept and fear being called oathbreakers; a character who shows the signet, or who tells them the truth of the fresco (room 13), and succeeds on a DC 16 Charisma (Persuasion) check makes them lie back down, and they will not rise against that party again.

Treasure: the Fallen King's Signet, in a skull's mouth in the niche above the middle bier.

Exits: Drowned Chapel (4, door), The Prince's Vault (12, arch and open passage). The door in the middle of the south side opens into the middle of the north side of the Drowned Chapel. The arch in the middle of the west side opens onto a passage west that ends at an open passage into the middle of the east side of the Prince's Vault.

name: Hall of the Kneeling Knights
read: Beyond the bronze door a long hall stretches east, and a dark pool of still seawater fills the middle of it. Four stone knights kneel in a row along the north wall, heads bowed toward a carved stone dais at the west end. A ring of runes is cut into the floor around the dais, every one of them scorched black. Two tall bronze candle stands flank it, and small offerings of shells lie in a neat line at the edge of the ring, as if no one dared step inside.
notes:
Here the drowned Legion came up out of the sea and held their King under the water of the pool until he died. The runes of the dais were cut by the tide-monks to bind his oath to this place.

Trap: Oathbreaker's Ring

  • Trigger: a creature enters the west 20 ft of the hall, wall to wall, around the rune-ringed dais by the bronze door. A party that opens the bronze door steps straight into it.
  • Find: DC 16 Wisdom (Perception) or Intelligence (Arcana) notices the ring of scorched runes, that all four knights kneel toward it, and that the shell offerings stop at its edge.
  • Effect: DC 16 Wisdom saving throw [[/save wis 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 psychic]] on a failure, half on a success. The runes blaze and the voices of the dead Legion roar Kneel! On a failure the creature also has the Frightened condition until the end of its next turn.
  • Disarm or avoid: Kneel: a creature that crosses the area on its knees (each foot costs 1 extra foot) does not trigger it. Otherwise scratch out a rune (DC 16 Intelligence (Arcana) check) or end it with Dispel Magic (DC 16).
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Hall of the Fallen Legion (5, locked bronze door), Tomb of the Fallen King (15, stairs and arch). The huge bronze door in the middle of the west side opens into the middle of the east side of the Hall of the Fallen Legion. The stairs at the west end of the south side go down to a short passage south that ends at an arch into the middle of the west side of the Tomb of the Fallen King.

name: Monk's Grotto
read: The sea washes into the north end of this grotto, and an iron brazier burns warm beside a monk's sleeping mat. Against the south wall stands a small stone shrine with candles and shells on it. A man in a grey robe lies on the floor, bound with rope and bleeding. Beside him, on a stool, are laid out hobgoblin torture tools and a water jug, and hobgoblins in robes stand over him.
notes:
The shrine of the Brothers of the Ebb, the tide-monks who kept the tomb. The man is Brother Tamsin, the last of them, mortally wounded. The devastators are torturing him for the words that open the bronze door (room 5). The brazier lights the grotto.

Encounter: 3 Hobgoblin Devastators stay spread out at range and blast the party, the last one threatening to kill the monk if the fight turns. Talk: they want the door's secret and fear going back to Vrask without it; a character who claims to bring the words from Vrask and succeeds on a DC 16 Charisma (Deception) check sends them off to room 5, leaving the monk.

The monk. Brother Tamsin is at 1 Hit Point and dying of his wounds. Any healing, or a DC 15 Wisdom (Medicine) check, keeps him talking; Lesser Restoration or more powerful healing saves him, otherwise he dies within the hour. He tells the party: the King's true name, Morvane, opens the bronze door; the four bronze urns in the tomb hold the King's drowned oath, and holy water from the Chapel of the Tide (room 11) destroys an urn; and the King betrayed his Legion, not the other way round. He gives them his sea-cloak, the Cloak of the Manta Ray, freely; he will not need it again.

Treasure: a Potion of Healing among the hobgoblin supplies on the stool, and the Cloak of the Manta Ray (Brother Tamsin's gift).

Exits: Flooded Antechamber (2, arch, barred gate and stairs), Hall of Offerings (3, arch, barred gate and stairs), Drowned Chapel (4, arch, barred gate and open passage). The arch in the middle of the east side opens onto a passage that runs east, north and east again to a barred iron gate (barred from the far side; it can be lifted from here with a DC 15 Strength (Athletics) check). Beyond it the passage meets a north–south passage: south, stairs go down into the middle of the north side of the Flooded Antechamber; north, it reaches a junction with stairs east up into the Hall of Offerings and an open passage west into the Drowned Chapel.

name: Guardian Antechamber
read: Two stone guardian statues stand on either side of an iron gate at the east end of the south wall, their stone swords lowered. A stone bench runs along the east wall. Three bulging hobgoblin loot sacks lie dumped on the floor beside a dropped torch and broken pottery.
notes:
The way to the tomb's side chambers. The hobgoblins have used it as a dump for loot they did not want to carry; the sacks hold bronze trinkets worth nothing to a level 10 party. The gate to the south is barred from this side with a spear through the bars.

No encounter.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Chamber of the Fresco (13, door), Hall of the Broken Carving (14, barred gate), Flooded Antechamber (2, door and arch), Hall of the Fallen Legion (5, door, two ways). The door in the middle of the west side opens into the middle of the east side of the Chamber of the Fresco. The barred gate at the east end of the south side opens into the middle of the north side of the Hall of the Broken Carving. The door in the middle of the north side opens onto a passage north to a flooded east–west corridor that runs east: past the Collapsing Passage south to the west door of the Hall of the Fallen Legion (see room 5), past the arch north into the Flooded Antechamber, and on to a passage south that ends at the north door of the Hall of the Fallen Legion.

name: Chapel of the Tide
read: Shell and coral offerings cover a seaweed-draped stone altar against the east wall of this small chapel. Before it, kneeling cushions lie around a carved stone font brimming with seawater. On the floor beside the font sits a rotten wicker basket, and inside it a small glass flask of clear water.
notes:
The tide-monks' chapel to the sea god. The flask is holy water, blessed by Brother Tamsin before the hobgoblins came; he hid it here, where the hobgoblins never looked.

No encounter.

Treasure: the Flask of Holy Water (story item) in the rotten basket. One use: poured on one of the King's bronze funeral urns (room 15) as an action, it destroys that urn outright; or thrown as a splash at an undead creature, it deals [[/damage 2d8 radiant]] damage.

Exits: Embalmers' Room (6, open passage and arch). The open passage in the middle of the west side leads to a passage west that ends at an arch into the middle of the east side of the Embalmers' Room.

name: The Prince's Vault
read: A stone sarcophagus stands in the middle of this small vault, and old coins lie scattered around it on the floor. Against the middle of the west wall sits an iron-bound chest, and the stone around its lock is stained a crusted green. A helmet rests on a stand beside two bronze urns, and on a shelf lies a folded, faded cape.
notes:
The tomb of the King's son, Prince Aldo, who died of fever as a boy. The scattered coins are corroded copper, worth nothing. The tide-monks trapped the prince's chest against robbers.

Trap: The Prince's Chest

  • Trigger: a creature opens the iron-bound chest against the west wall, poisoning those standing in the squares in front of it.
  • Find: DC 16 Intelligence (Investigation) finds the needle in the keyhole and sees that the green stain round the lock is dried poison.
  • Effect: DC 16 Constitution saving throw [[/save con 16]]; [[/damage 10d10 poison]] on a failure, half on a success. A needle springs from the lock and a green mist puffs out. On a failure the creature also has the Poisoned condition.
  • Disarm or avoid: Jam or remove the needle (DC 16 Dexterity check with thieves' tools), or open the lid from outside the area with a pole or rope.
  • Automation: a hidden Monk's Active Tiles tile asks the entering character for the save through Monk's TokenBar and applies the damage (half on a success). Re-enable the tile to reset the trap.

No encounter.

Treasure: 400 gp in the chest. The folded cape on the shelf is a Cloak of Protection, the prince's.

Exits: Ossuary of the Honour Guard (7, open passage and arch). The open passage in the middle of the east side leads to a passage east that ends at an arch into the middle of the west side of the Ossuary of the Honour Guard.

name: Chamber of the Fresco
read: A long stone bench runs down this narrow chamber, set for someone to lie on and look up at the ceiling. Candle stubs stand in the corners. A broken hand mirror, a few scattered bones and a small offering bowl lie on the floor. Above you, the ceiling is covered in a painted fresco, too dark to make out.
notes:
The court of Skerrow painted their King's story here. The fresco glows faintly violet when anyone looks at it in light. It shows the truth the island forgot: King Hadrek swearing to live or die with his Legion; the raiders' ships; the King barring the sea-gate with his court safe behind him while the Legion dies on the beach outside; and the courtiers applauding him. Around the crown in the first scene, the King's true name, Morvane, is written in the waves (DC 15 Intelligence (History) to read the old letters).

Encounter: 3 Court Shades, the courtiers who cheered, rise from the shadows the moment anyone looks at the fresco and attack those who have seen it, slipping through the walls and striking from the dark. Talk: they want the truth kept hidden and fear their names being spoken; a character who swears never to tell what they saw and succeeds on a DC 15 Charisma (Deception or Persuasion) check makes them sink back into the ceiling.

Treasure: none.

Exits: Guardian Antechamber (10, door). The door in the middle of the east side opens into the middle of the west side of the Guardian Antechamber.

name: Hall of the Broken Carving
read: The great carving that once covered the south wall of this hall has been smashed to pieces, and its rubble lies heaped along the foot of the wall. Broken statue heads stare up from the floor beside a toppled stone plinth. Hobgoblin hammers and chisels are scattered among the stone, next to pots of red paint.
notes:
The carving showed the Fallen Legion's oath, the Legion kneeling before their King. The hobgoblins smashed it hunting for hidden treasure, and daubed their red war marks over what was left. Nothing can be read from it now.

No encounter.

Treasure: a Potion of Climbing in a hobgoblin's tool roll among the hammers and chisels.

Exits: Guardian Antechamber (10, barred gate). The barred gate in the middle of the north side opens into the east end of the south side of the Guardian Antechamber.

name: Tomb of the Fallen King
read: Cold blue witch-light hangs around a black stone sarcophagus in the centre of this round tomb, its lid thrown aside. Four tall bronze funeral urns stand around it, to the north, east, south and west, each beaded with seawater. Gold coins and grave goods lie scattered among strands of seaweed, and against the wall stands a small bronze throne. In the east wall, steps lead down into black water.
notes:
The end of the sepulcher. The Fallen King, King Hadrek of Skerrow, true name Morvane, rises from his sarcophagus as the party enters, water running from his crown. The last of his Legion stands guard over him. The witch-light gives dim light across the room.

Encounter: The Fallen King and 1 Barrow Wight. The King is an Epic Boss; the wight blocks the way to the urns while the King fights. Talk: the King wants to be free of his oath and fears his crime being spoken aloud; he offers the party the gold and his mace if they swear fealty and leave the urns whole (a DC 18 Wisdom (Insight) check shows he will kill them once they turn their backs). A character who names him Morvane Oathbreaker and succeeds on a DC 18 Charisma (Intimidation) check makes the wight turn on the King.

The urns. The four bronze funeral urns hold the King's drowned oath. Each urn has AC 15, 25 Hit Points and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage; or a creature within 5 ft of an urn can take an action to smash or tip it over with a DC 16 Strength (Athletics) check; or pouring the Flask of Holy Water (room 11) on an urn destroys it outright. Each urn destroyed deals [[/damage 2d10 radiant]] damage to the King. While at least one urn stands, the King has Epic Boss Resistance; when the fourth is destroyed, he loses it.

The stairs down. The stairs in the middle of the east side lead nowhere useful: 30 ft down they are flooded to the ceiling and sealed by rubble.

Treasure: 500 gp in grave goods scattered round the room, and the Mace of Disruption in the King's sarcophagus.

Exits: Hall of the Kneeling Knights (8, arch and stairs). The arch in the middle of the west side opens onto a short passage north that climbs stairs into the west end of the south side of the Hall of the Kneeling Knights. The stairs down in the middle of the east side are flooded and blocked (see above).
